learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to confidently handle technical terminology and physical quantities (e.g., energy and power, efficiency and utilization rates, from primary energy to final energy use).

Students are able to describe the fundamental mechanisms of climate change, the CO2 cycle, their relevant influencing factors, and their effects. Terms such as tipping points (CTPs), solar constant, greenhouse gas effect, and many more can be used confidently by students.
Based on these insights into energy policy, students can discuss and evaluate possible developments and derive consequences for corporate decisions.

Students can fundamentally understand the functioning of relevant technologies for climate-friendly energy supply (wind, biogas, PV, geothermal, hydropower) as well as climate-friendly use (e.g., electric vehicles, heat pumps) and storage (hydrogen, battery).
Through rough estimations of the potentials of renewable energies, students can classify them into the overall supply system and recognize interactions.
Students can evaluate new technologies (future technologies), also for their future sustainable role in different organizational units, considering sustainability aspects.
Students can correctly apply the physical principles for environmental and energy technology using the discussed examples.
Students can apply their strengthened understanding of systemic relationships.
Students can independently and in a team familiarize themselves with new topics related to environmental and future technologies and present them in a plenary session.

syllabus_topics: Climate change, greenhouse gas balance, carbon cycle, tipping points, solar constant, temperature increase, influencing factors on temperature
National energy transition in an international context, basics of energy policy
Energy balance, energy conservation, forms of energy, efficiency, utilization factor

Technical fundamentals (energy, power, final energy (focus: electricity, heat, energy for mobility), key figures such as efficiency, utilization factor, coefficient of performance (COP), annual performance factor)
Renewable energy generation (focus: wind, PV, biogas, geothermal, hydropower)
Energy-efficient energy supply (heat pumps, combined electricity and heat supply)
Efficient energy use (insulation, electric vehicles, heat pumps)
Energy storage technologies (battery technologies, heat storage, hydrogen as an energy carrier)
Outlook on (possible) future technologies (e.g., marine pumped storage, water battery, Power to Liquid, CO2 storage, EE-Methanol, etc.)
assessment_rules: The assessment is a 90-minute written examination. Up to 9 bonus points can be achieved by a successful presentation of a future technology. Active participation in the discussion is required to receive bonus points.
